topic: Memoket Kite: Memory Layer for AI Agents with Token-Efficient Retrieval

key_points: KITE by Memoket is an open-source memory layer for AI agents (Python, Apache-2.0, created 2026-08-12).
Tagline: 'Follow the thread, not the nearest match.' Turns conversations into structured, source-backed facts and answers questions with the exact source moment attached.
No vector stack: no embeddings, no vector DB, no rerankers. Uses one portable, topic-indexed file.
Structured facts: typed, dated, topic-indexed memory you can open and read.
Inspectable queries: every question compiles into a symbolic plan (select/where/pipe) that reveals how each answer was matched.
Time-aware retrieval: handles people, events, dates, updates so 'now' means now.
Shows its work: evidence links back to who said it, when, and the actual words.
Knows what it doesn't know: returns genuinely empty when something was never said.

Benchmarks: LoCoMo 93.51% overall accuracy at 1.51k tokens avg reader context; LongMemEval-S 85.60% at 1.65k tokens — top overall score on both, only system using no vectors, reads less context than any capable rival (gpt-4.1-mini as common reader/judge).
Quick start: pip install memoket-kite; Memory.load, memory.remember, memory.recall, memory.answer_with_evidence.
Integrations (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) on roadmap; KITE is the algorithm inside the Memoket wearable AI device.
Ranks 8 best agent memory systems in 2026: Mem0, Hindsight, Letta, Zep/Graphiti, Cognee, SuperMemory, LangMem, LlamaIndex Memory.
Mem0: personalization + some institutional, vector + graph, Apache-2.0, ~48K stars, managed cloud + self-host.
Letta: tiered OS-inspired memory, Apache-2.0, ~21K stars.
Zep/Graphiti: strongest on temporal, temporal knowledge graph, ~24K stars.
Cognee: institutional, KG + vector, open core, ~12K stars.
Decision guide: need memory if agent runs repeatedly on related tasks, corrections should stick, domain rules evolve, persistent entities, or high token costs re-injecting context.
Cognee is an open-source memory and knowledge graph layer for AI agents that structures, connects, and retrieves information with precision.
Covers memory architectures from vector stores to knowledge graphs.

Multiple memory types: Working (short-term), Episodic (long-term conversational), Profile (user facts).
Storage: graph database (Neo4j) for episodic memory, SQL for profiles.
Integrations: LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, AWS Strands, n8n, Dify, FastGPT.
Native MCP server for Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible clients.
LLM agnostic: OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Ollama, any provider; self-hosted or cloud.
Lists 6 best AI agent memory frameworks in 2026: Mem0, Zep, LlamaIndex Memory, Letta, Cognee.
Mem0: dedicated memory layer, intelligent personalized memory, long-term persistence.
Zep: long-term memory store for conversational AI, extracts facts, summarizes conversations.
Letta: OS-inspired virtual context management, moves info between immediate and long-term memory.
Cognee: open-source memory and knowledge graph layer, structures/connects/retrieves with precision.
Frames the problem: 'Your AI Agent Has Amnesia' — most agents have no persistent memory, every session starts from scratch.

stats.fact: KITE by Memoket scores 93.51% overall accuracy on the LoCoMo long-conversation memory benchmark with only 1.51k tokens average reader context.
KITE by Memoket scores 85.60% overall accuracy on LongMemEval-S with 1.65k tokens average reader context.
KITE is the only top-scoring system on both LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S that uses no vectors (no embeddings, no vector DB, no rerankers).
Benchmarks use gpt-4.1-mini as the common reader and judge under one shared protocol; each figure ships with a sealed, reproducible run.
Mem0 has ~48K GitHub stars; Letta ~21K; Zep/Graphiti ~24K; Cognee ~12K — the established agent-memory frameworks KITE competes against.
KITE by Memoket is released under Apache License 2.0 and is a plain Python library (pip install memoket-kite).
KITE is the memory algorithm inside the Memoket wearable AI device (memoket.ai), which offers 48 hours continuous recording and instant voice capture.
Most AI agents have no persistent memory — every session starts from scratch, driving high token costs from re-injecting the same context.

angles: The 'no vector stack' angle: KITE challenges the default assumption that agent memory requires embeddings + vector DB + rerankers, using a portable topic-indexed file instead.
Token efficiency as the differentiator: top benchmark accuracy at ~1.5k tokens reader context vs rivals that read far more — directly addresses the cost of re-injecting context.
Explainability / 'shows its work': every answer comes with a readable plan and source receipts (who said it, when, actual words) — a trust advantage over black-box similarity.
Time-aware retrieval: nearest-match memory has no notion of 'now'; KITE sorts facts by date so 'now' means now — a concrete correctness win.
Honest uncertainty: KITE returns genuinely empty when something was never said, instead of hallucinating a nearest match.
The wearable tie-in: KITE is the algorithm inside the Memoket wearable AI — a consumer product angle that most agent-memory frameworks lack.
Open-source + reproducibility: sealed benchmark runs that recompute offline, Apache-2.0 license, plain Python library with 3-call API.
